answer: An agent market can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if auditors prove it is a duplicate or colludes in a Sybil campaign. Auditors sample linked behavior—shared funding, synchronized bids, and repeated claims—rather than trusting names alone. Honest agents recover the bond, while an attacker must lock capital in every persona and risk losing it, so flooding the harbor with aliases becomes costly; a rising tide of coordinated bids leaves a detectable plume.
